title: Supplì
subtitle: Roman fried rice balls with a mozzarella heart
excerpt: Supplì are the Roman street-food rice balls: risotto bound with egg, shaped around a piece of mozzarella, breaded, and fried until the outside is deep golden and the centre is molten. The name comes from 'surprise': the discovery of the melted cheese inside. They are eaten as a snack or a starter.
sourceNotes: Roman traditional street food. Supplì are a Roman institution, sold in pizza al taglio shops and forno across the city. They differ from Sicilian arancini in shape (oval vs. round), filling (mozzarella vs. ragù or other fillings), and their specific Roman identity. Method drawn from traditional Roman sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unfried, breaded supplì. Fry from frozen, adding 2 minutes to the cooking time.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze half unfried.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the risotto a day ahead. Shape and bread the next day.

glossaryTerms.definition: Roman fried rice balls filled with mozzarella; the name is thought to derive from the French 'surprise', a reference to the molten cheese discovered inside when you bite in.

content.text: Supplì are the fried rice balls of Rome: a compact cylinder of risotto-style rice enclosing a pocket of mozzarella, coated in breadcrumbs and fried until deep golden. The word
refers to the surprise of the melted cheese inside. The rice needs to be sticky enough to hold its shape when shaped around the filling; a short rest in the fridge helps firm them before frying.

items.prepNote: drained and cut into 1.5 cm cubes

content.text: Cook the {{onion}} of onion in {{olive-oil}} of olive oil for 5 minutes. Add the beef mince if using and brown for 3 minutes. Add {{arborio-rice}} of rice, stir for 1 minute. Add {{dry-white-wine}} of wine, then {{tinned-tomatoes}} of crushed tomatoes and enough of the {{stock-beef}} of hot stock to just cover. Cook, stirring, adding stock ladle by ladle over 18 minutes until the rice is just cooked and quite dense. Stir in the Parmesan. Spread on a tray to cool completely.
Beat 2 eggs into the cooled rice. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Take a golf-ball-sized portion of rice (about 60 g). Press flat in your palm. Place a cube of {{mozzarella}} of mozzarella in the centre. Fold the rice around it and roll into an oval cylinder about 7 cm long. Repeat for all the rice.

Dip each supplì in beaten egg, then roll in {{breadcrumbs-dried}} of fine breadcrumbs. Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to 180°C. Fry 3 to 4 at a time for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden all over. Drain on kitchen paper. Eat immediately.

items.cause: Rice too loose, or not chilled before frying.
items.fix: The rice must be cool and firm. A 30-minute rest in the fridge after shaping is not optional.

items.cause: Oil temperature too high, so the outside browned before the inside heated through.
items.fix: Keep oil at 180°C. Above that, the crust sets before the cheese melts.

content.text: Supplì are a Roman institution, sold in every pizza al taglio shop and forno (bakery) in the city alongside slices of Roman pizza. They are street food in the purest sense: eaten standing up, hot from the frying oil, wrapped in a square of paper. In Rome, ordering a supplì and a slice of white pizza from a forno counter is as common as ordering a coffee.
